tip.title: Nominalisierung in speech
tip.body: Turning verbs into nouns sounds more precise: ausreichend schlafen → ausreichender Schlaf, sich ernähren → die Ernährung. Use it sparingly in speech – one noun phrase per sentence is enough. When giving advice, soften it with an Es wäre vielleicht gut, wenn … and a warm, rising tone instead of a commanding Du musst …

lessons.title: Regrets and hindsight
lessons.goal: Talk about past decisions, regrets and what would have happened otherwise.

tip.title: Konjunktiv II Vergangenheit
tip.body: For unreal past situations use hätte/wäre + Partizip II: Ich hätte früher zum Arzt gehen sollen. Wenn ich mich aufgewärmt hätte, wäre das nicht passiert. With modal verbs, the double infinitive goes at the end: hätte … gehen sollen. Stress hätte or wäre – that's where the regret sits.

lessons.title: Je … desto: the more, the better
lessons.goal: Link cause and effect with je … desto / umso.

tip.title: Two comparatives, two word orders
tip.body: Je + comparative starts a subordinate clause, so its verb goes to the end: Je mehr ich mich bewege … The second half starts with desto or umso + comparative, and the verb follows immediately: … desto besser schlafe ich. In short sayings you can drop the second verb: Je früher, desto besser.

phrases.n: The more I move, the better I sleep.

phrases.n: The less sugar I eat, the fitter I feel.

lessons.title: Your lifestyle
lessons.goal: Talk freely about your health habits and give tactful advice.

culture.title: Krankschreibung and Kur
culture.body: If you're ill in Germany, you need a doctor's sick note (Krankschreibung, now sent electronically to employers) by the fourth day off at the latest — some employers want it from day one. Doctors can also prescribe a Kur or Reha: several weeks in a spa town, often with Bad in its name like Bad Kissingen, largely paid for by insurance. Austria has a similar Kur tradition.
